gedhitamano.meaning_2: with a mind clinging (to); with a greedy mind (for); whose mind is attached (to)
gedhitamano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound qualifying the non-giver; locative āmisasmiṃ depends on gedhita. Nominative singular in the verse.
gedhitamano.example_1: Adātā gedhitamano āmisasmiṃ, dussīlyena yamavisayamhi patto.
gedhitamano.translation_1: a non-giver, with a mind clinging to worldly things. Because of my immorality, I have arrived in the realm of Yama.

ummattarūpova.meaning_2: looking like a madman; as if insane; appearing crazy
ummattarūpova.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text joined with eva and iva as ummattarūpova (ummattarūpo + iva). Nominative singular in all three verses, used in similes.
ummattarūpova.example_1: 46. ‘‘ Kiṃ nu ummattarūpova, lāyitvā haritaṃ tiṇaṃ;
ummattarūpova.translation_1: 46. “Are you mad, that having cut fresh grass,
ummattarūpova.example_2: 209. ‘‘ Kiṃ nu ummattarūpova, kevalaṃ dvārakaṃ imaṃ;
ummattarūpova.translation_2: 209. “Why are you acting like a madman, wandering all over this city of Dvārakā,

bhojanatthike.meaning_2: wanting food; desiring food; seeking food
bhojanatthike.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of bhojana (food) + atthika (wanting; from attha, desire). In the text it is accusative plural, agreeing with yācanake (beggars).
bhojanatthike.translation_1: 285. “Seeing there the beggars who had arrived, desiring food;

ramitomhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ramito + amhi; 1st person singular present of ramati with the enclitic amhi, 'I have dallied with you'. The participle ramita is a separate entry.
ramitomhi.example_1: 367. ‘‘ Bhuttā amānusā kāmā, ramitomhi tayā saha;
ramitomhi.translation_1: 367. “Celestial sensual pleasures have been enjoyed, and I have dallied with you.

vimānamāruyha.meaning_2: having ascended the mansion; having climbed into the palace
vimānamāruyha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vimānaṃ (accusative singular of vimāna 2.1) and the gerund āruyha. The compound verb vimānaṃ āruhati would alternatively be analysed as a compound verb.
vimānamāruyha.translation_1: 439. “O mighty goddess, having ascended this mansion (vimāna) with lapis lazuli pillars, delightful, luminous, and of varied design;

saṃsavako.meaning_2: name of a hell; Saṃsavaka hell; the hell of excrement and urine
saṃsavako.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a hell (sataporisa, a hundred fathoms deep). Nominative singular in the text. The PEU split saṃ + su + ṇvu is uncertain; the name probably relates to √sav (flow) or saṃsava (excrement and urine).
saṃsavako.translation_1: 723. “This is called Saṃsavaka, deep, a hell of suffering,
saṃsavako.example_2: Kena saṃsavako laddho, gambhīro sataporiso ’’ ti.
saṃsavako.translation_2: For which I have attained this Saṃsavaka hell, deep and a hundred fathoms?”

morahatthehi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental plural in the text: fanned with peacock feathers. Comms gloss morahattha as a fan or bundle of peacock tail-feathers.
morahatthehi.example_1: Bījitaṅgā [vījitaṅgā (sī. syā.)] morahatthehi, kule jātā yasassino.
morahatthehi.translation_1: fanned with peacock feathers, born into renowned families, they rejoice.

kiṭakasamā.meaning_2: like iron plates; resembling iron sheets
kiṭakasamā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of kiṭaka (iron plate) and sama (like). In the text it is plural nominative agreeing with vatthā: 'let your garments be like iron plates'.
kiṭakasamā.example_1: Etaṃ te paralokasmiṃ hotu, vatthā ca te kiṭakasamā bhavantu ’;
kiṭakasamā.translation_1: Let this be yours in the next world, and let your garments be iron plates.’

ubbarīti.meaning_2: Ubbarī (a proper name; name of a queen; name of a woman)
ubbarīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text ubbarīti = ubbarī + iti, the -iti being the quotation marker; entry is for the name itself. Listed among proper names in the verse.
ubbarīti.example_2: Dve seṭṭhī tunnavāyo ca, uttara [vihāra (sabbattha)] suttakaṇṇa [sopāna (sabbattha)] ubbarīti.
ubbarīti.translation_2: Two seṭṭhīs, the tailor, and Uttara, Sutta, Kaṇṇa, and Ubbarī.

muḷhassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text muḷhassa is genitive singular, qualifying the person to whom the path was not declared; from √muh with past participle suffix -ta, written with ḷ.

pavīsati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Text reads pavīsati with a long ī, a metrical lengthening of pavisati; 3rd singular present. Takes an accusative object (gāmaṃ, gehaṃ).
